exposure: Wearable sensor data (resting heart rate, physical activity, sleep patterns)
cohort: The study included 99 participants (aged >=16 years, residing in the United States) who experienced a live birth pregnancy, with data collected from three months pre-pregnancy to six months postpartum via their own wearable devices.
finding: Wearable sensors effectively track physiological and behavioral changes during pregnancy, such as RHR fluctuations and sleep patterns, which align strongly with expected hormonal shifts, and distinct RHR patterns were observed in pregnancies ending in adverse outcomes.
